_: THE SWEEP THAT SAYS THE LOCKFILE LAW IS NOT VACUOUS — run it from the
A SECOND SWEEP BESIDE `injection-sweep.json` BECAUSE IT RUNS A DIFFERENT
SUITE. That one breaks the READING rules and watches `ci-plan`'s own tests;
this one breaks THIS REPOSITORY — a flag in a workflow, a flag in a hook,
the ownership answer the workspace lister gives — and watches the gate that
walks the tree. Neither could be folded into the other: a manifest names one
test command, and a sweep that ran both suites for every injection would
spend the expensive one proving things the cheap one already proves.
THE FIRST FOUR ARE THE DEFECT ITSELF. On the tree this law arrived in, THIRTY
cargo commands resolved without `--locked`, so each of these puts one of them
back and asks whether anybody notices.
THE SUITE IS ADDRESSED AS A MODULE OF `all` AND NOT AS A TARGET. R1171 folded
seventy-six of the cli crate's test files into one binary, this file among
them; a `--test locked_resolution_smoke` after that commit is a name cargo
refuses outright, which takes the WHOLE sweep with it. The trailing filter
reproduces exactly the population this command had before the fold.

injections.name: a-workflow-step-resolves-freely
injections.why: this is the shape the gate was written for: a step that resolves without the flag rewrites a disagreeing lockfile before any later step in the same job can be asked about one

injections.name: a-git-hook-resolves-freely
injections.why: the hooks are the half of this repository's checks that no gate's population reached until R1115, and a developer meets them before CI does

injections.name: the-lister-stops-pinning-anything
injections.why: the workspace lister assembles its commands at runtime, so a flag can leave every one of them at once and no reading of its text would show it — this is why the gate reads what the lister PRINTS

injections.name: a-script-resolves-freely
injections.why: `scripts/gc` builds the whole workspace to warm the artifacts it is about to sweep; a free resolve there rewrites the root lockfile in the working tree of whoever ran it

injections.name: every-workspace-is-this-repositorys-to-pin
injections.why: `studio` resolves against the sibling `pinion` checkout. An ownership answer that never says so puts `--locked` on a workspace another repository's commit can break, and leaves the lockfile it cannot pin looking like one it should keep

injections.name: the-measured-fixture-agrees-with-its-manifest
injections.why: every claim about what cargo does to a lockfile rests on that fixture actually HOLDING a disagreement; if the version matches, a free resolve leaves the file alone and the measurement records `leaves it alone` for every subcommand there is

injections.name: the-tracked-shell-is-not-in-the-population
injections.why: three sources are bolted together here and dropping one takes the count down without taking it to zero — fifty compliant workflow commands read exactly like a clean repository, which is why the non-vacuity floor is per source rather than a total. R1277 ADDED A FOURTH RED AND IT IS NOT ABOUT ARMS: `script_files` refuses an empty answer itself, so every law over this population dies where it is assembled rather than where it is asked

injections.name: the-sixth-sources-flag-goes-away
injections.why: R1262 — the defect this population exists to catch, in the source that had never been in it: a free resolve over a tracked manifest REWRITES a lockfile that disagrees with it instead of failing on it, and this one is issued by a gate whose whole job is to report on the tree

injections.name: a-resolving-command-declines-to-name-its-tree
injections.why: R1262 — THE THIRD ARM'S OBLIGATION. `WhereverTheCallerPoints` is the arm that does not name a tree, and what it owes in exchange is a command that cannot touch a lockfile; a `cargo build` declared there is a resolve over a workspace nobody named, which is the arm being used as an exemption

injections.name: a-command-with-a-hole-in-it-is-judged-as-if-whole
injections.why: R1262 — an `.args(expr)` hands over an unknown NUMBER of words, so a flag may be inside it; judging such a command answers about words nobody read, and the answer arrives with the same confidence as every other one in the tally. R1277 ADDED A FOURTH RED AND IT IS THE OTHER DIRECTION OF THE LIST: reading holes as words makes all SEVEN sites listed as unreadable readable at once, and a list still claiming a limit this repository no longer has is a claim as wrong as a missing entry

injections.name: a-metadata-census-is-treated-as-a-resolution
injections.why: R1262 — `cargo metadata --no-deps` resolves nothing, which THIS SUITE has measured since the round that wrote it and the verdict function did not know. A judge without that fact demands `--locked` of commands the flag can do nothing for, which is a law satisfied by a word with no effect

injections.name: a-measurement-that-could-not-run-answers-anyway
injections.why: R1262 — a command that fails for its own reasons leaves the lockfile alone, and reading that as `this subcommand does not resolve` produced a WRONG entry rather than a missing one: `cargo rustdoc` refused to pick a target, touched nothing, and was recorded as a subcommand `--locked` has no work to do for

injections.name: pinning-wherever-it-points-is-read-as-owning-nothing
injections.why: the fourth arm asks to be judged as though every tree were one to pin, which is the strictest reading and the only safe one when nobody named the tree; read the other way it becomes an exemption, and the gate that runs `cargo check` over whatever workspace it is handed goes back to rewriting the lockfile it was pointed at

injections.name: the-gate-pointed-at-a-workspace-resolves-it-freely
injections.why: `item-citations` runs `cargo check` over whichever workspace it is handed — this repository under the side gate — and without the flag a lockfile that disagrees with its manifests is REWRITTEN rather than reported, with every check after it in the same run reading the repaired file

injections.name: a-site-whose-words-depend-on-the-path-is-left-unjudged
injections.why: before R1265 a site written with a conditional word was one command nobody could read, and this law said nothing about it — which is the same silence as a clean answer. Dropping the paths again takes twelve commands out of the population, one of them the `RepairsWhatItShouldReport` R1265 found. THE ANCHOR MOVED IN R1268 and the injection followed it rather than being retired: the expansion used to live in this law, which is exactly why two of the other three laws never saw those commands, and it now lives in `RustSpawns::every_command` where every law reads it. R1277 ADDED A SECOND RED AND IT IS THE CLEAREST EVIDENCE THAT THE NEW LAW REACHES ARMS R1271 NEVER ASKED ABOUT: five sites leave reach unnamed across THREE arms — `tool_pin_smoke::run_in` (ThisRepository), `unrun-tests::has_library` (WhereverTheCallerPoints) and the three PinnedWhenItIsOurs ones

injections.name: a-runtime-subcommand-is-read-as-one-a-table-knows
injections.why: this suite's own measurement fixture loops over every subcommand cargo has, so it writes `$subcommand`; classified as a subcommand a table can be keyed on, the law reports Unreadable and goes red on a fixture doing exactly what it should. R1277 ADDED A THIRD RED: the two fixtures whose subcommand is the loop's word become readable, so the list naming them as sites nobody can read is claiming a limit that just went away

injections.name: pinning-when-the-tree-is-ours-is-read-as-always-ours
injections.why: the fifth arm says the flag is present exactly where the lockfile is this repository's, so reading ownership off anything but the flag makes the path WITHOUT it a command that resolves one of ours freely — the defect this arm was introduced to name rather than hide

injections.name: a-site-that-pins-when-ours-spells-the-flag-on-every-path
injections.why: the arm's verdict half cannot fail, so its teeth are the site owing a CONDITIONAL flag: spelled unconditionally the declaration claims a condition the code does not have, and the arm becomes a way past the other four rather than a fifth answer

injections.name: a-site-that-declares-the-arm-and-issues-nothing-leaves-in-silence
injections.why: R1271, and this injection is the round's own subject. A law about an arm asks its COMMANDS, so a site whose words stop being readable issues none and drops out — and the law goes on passing over the sites that remain, which is a green meaning `two sites are fine` read as `this repository's sites are fine`. Measured: `stale-artifacts::apply` declares this arm and issued no judged command at all until the list its helper returns was read. Taking the hop away puts the tree back in that state, and the count of DECLARING sites is what notices

injections.name: a-command-carries-a-declaration-and-names-no-site
injections.why: R1277 — reach is counted in SITES and a command's `origin` is not one: a command read at a call site is attributed to that caller, so one site reached through five callers has five origins. The pairing of `declared` with `site` is what makes the count askable at all, and a declaration whose site went missing would leave every arm with fewer sites answering for it and nothing saying so

injections.name: an-arm-the-chain-skips-is-an-arm-nobody-asks-about
injections.why: R1277 — `Declared::arms` is a successor chain, so the compiler keeps it exhaustive over the ENUM and cannot keep it exhaustive over the CHAIN: a link that skips one builds fine, and the law over every arm then simply never asks about that one. That is the silence this law exists to close, one level up, so the arms asked about are held against the arms sites were found declaring

injections.name: a-site-listed-as-unreadable-is-one-anybody-can-read
injections.why: R1277 — the list of sites nobody can read is the half a green run does not cover, so a list that may hold an entry no site answers to is a limit this repository claims and does not have. The direction matters as much as the other: a reader that got better, or a site that was deleted, leaves an entry standing that says a gate is blind where it is not

injections.name: a-site-that-issues-nothing-is-in-no-bucket-either
injections.why: R1277 — a site that issues no command is answered by the bucket it lands in, which is where the reason a reader can print comes from. A site in NEITHER bucket has left every number this walk keeps at the same time, which is the conservation failure `read_but_unanswered` exists for one level down, and the law has to say so rather than read the absence as nothing to report

injections.name: a-relay-adds-the-pin-the-other-site-chose-not-to
injections.why: R1278 — a relay's whole claim is that the verdict was recorded where the words were written, and `--locked` is the word that verdict is read from. Adding it pins what the other site chose not to pin, which makes the answer here a different answer from the one being inherited

injections.name: a-relay-adds-the-word-this-repositorys-verdict-cannot-see
injections.why: R1278, AND IT IS THE ENTRY IN `WORDS_A_RELAY_MAY_NOT_ADD` THAT IS NOT DERIVED FROM WHAT `lock_verdict` READS. `--frozen` IS `--locked --offline`, and `is_the_pin` matches the literal `--locked` only — so a relay adding it pins the other site's command in a word this repository's verdict function is blind to. Without this injection those two entries would be decoration

injections.name: a-relay-points-the-command-at-a-tree-of-its-own
injections.why: R1278 — `--manifest-path` is the second of the three words a verdict is read from, and it is the most plausible mistake of the three: a gate that wants to be sure which workspace it is asking about adds it, and the command is then over a different tree from the one whose verdict is being inherited

injections.name: a-relay-writes-its-own-subcommand-first
injections.why: R1278 — the FIRST word a relay hands over has to be the relayed list, because that is what makes the subcommand the other site's. A literal in front of it and the command is running something this site chose, over words that were judged as something else

injections.name: a-relay-with-no-hole-in-it-relays-nothing
injections.why: R1278 — a site declaring the relay arm and handing over a word list this reader can FINISH is not relaying anything, and it is the one break that would otherwise be silent: such a site leaves the conditional and carried buckets altogether, so a law that only walked those buckets would hold over fewer sites and say nothing. That is R1271's silence, and the equality against `declaring` is what catches it

injections.name: the-relay-arms-verdict-is-not-the-one-already-recorded
injections.why: R1278 — the whole content of the arm is that the verdict is the one recorded where the words are written, so a `lock_verdict` that answers something else for it has taken the arm's meaning away while leaving its name. Answering `ResolvesNothing` is the specific wrong answer worth injecting: it is a PASS, so nothing else in this file would notice

injections.name: the-arm-a-relay-left-stops-refusing-what-it-documents
injections.why: R1278 — half of this round's measurement is that `WhereverTheCallerPoints` REFUSES a command that resolves, which is what made the four relays' old declaration false. If that arm stopped refusing, the old declaration would have been fine all along and the round's reason would be gone — and nothing else in this file would go red, because the six sites that legitimately declare that arm resolve nothing and pass either way

injections.name: a-measurement-pins-on-every-path
injections.why: R1279 — the one arm where the pin is a VARIABLE rather than a forbidden word owes that the variable vary. A fixture that pins unconditionally is asserting a difference rather than measuring one, and it is the half that would otherwise be silent: unconditional words are words this reader can finish, so the site leaves both buckets and a law walking only the buckets would hold over fewer sites and say nothing. R1271's shape, caught by the equality against `declaring`

injections.name: a-measurement-pins-on-no-path-at-all
injections.why: R1279 — the other direction of the same obligation, and it stays inside the bucket (R1280's third arm leaves another conditional word there) so it exercises the word-reading half rather than the equality: a site whose conditional words include no pin has no free-versus-pinned difference in it, and the arm it declares is a claim that it does

injections.name: the-planted-lockfile-is-read-as-a-tree-to-refuse
injections.why: R1279 — the arm exists because neither boolean fits: read as ours the free path is `RepairsWhatItShouldReport`, read as not-ours the pinned path is `PinsWhatItDoesNotOwn`. Answering one of those instead of the arm's own verdict puts the measurement back in the position that made its old declaration false, and the only thing that would notice is the law that compares the two arms

injections.name: the-arm-the-measurement-left-stops-refusing-a-pin
injections.why: R1279 — half of this round's measurement is that `MadeByThisRun` REFUSES a command that pins, which is what made the fixture's old declaration false. If that arm read its tree as ours, the old declaration would have been fine all along and the round's reason would be gone

injections.name: the-third-arm-of-the-measurement-runs-without-its-flag
injections.why: R1280 — what licenses `ci_plan::is_the_pin` reading `--frozen` as the pin is not cargo's documentation but this fixture running both flags against a planted disagreement and asserting they act the same. An arm that forgets to add its own flag measures the FREE case twice and reports the equivalence it was supposed to test, which is the shape of every vacuous measurement: the answer arrives with the same confidence and is about nothing
